response:
The Terms of Service concern the **MindWell Sleep Study**, a research study examining the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.

Key provisions are outlined below:

* **Purpose**: The study aims to examine how well a sleep-tracking app helps people with insomnia.
* **Participation**: You'll wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
* **Risks and discomfort**: There's a **minimal risk** of skin irritation from the sensor strap.
* **Data usage**: De-identified data (data that doesn't directly identify you) may be shared with universities, but identifiable data (data directly tied to you) won't be shared outside the research team. This suggests your personal identifiable data is relatively safe.
* **Withdrawal**: You can withdraw from the study at any time without any penalties.
* **Compensation**: You'll receive $75 upon completing the study.
* **Support**: If you have questions, you can contact **IRB (Institutional Review Board)** via irb@example.edu.

The Terms of Service do not explicitly mention data storage or protection beyond de-identification, but this provision suggests some level of data security.
source_tos:
INFORMED CONSENT — MINDWELL SLEEP STUDY

1. PURPOSE. This study examines the effects of a sleep-tracking app on insomnia.
2. PROCEDURES. Participants wear a wrist sensor for 8 weeks and complete weekly surveys.
3. RISKS. Minimal risk: skin irritation from the sensor strap.
4. DATA. De-identified data may be shared with collaborating universities. Identifiable data will not be shared outside the research team.
5. WITHDRAWAL. You may withdraw at any time without penalty.
6. COMPENSATION. Participants receive $75 upon completion.
7. CONTACT. For questions contact the IRB at irb@example.edu.

**Service Name:** Google Terms of Service (2022)

**Summary:** These Terms of Service regulate the relationship between Google and its users, outlining the expectations and rules for using Google's products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to Google's products and services listed on its official terms page.
* **User-Submitted Content:** Google can use user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Google's published Privacy Policy sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most terms require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under the conditions described in the document.
* **Contact:** For questions, see Google's published legal contact information.

**Provisions to be aware of:**

* The requirement for **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, which may not offer the same level of protection as going to court. This means users may waive their right to participate in a class-action lawsuit.
* The **30-day opt-out window** for new accounts, which may be limited in its effectiveness.

Please note that the Terms of Service do not explicitly address topics like data ownership, intellectual property, or data portability. If you're concerned about any specific aspect, I recommend reviewing the document (available at https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105?hl=en-US) or reaching out to Google's support team.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GOOGLE TERMS OF SERVICE (2020 → 2022) (Effective 2022; replaces the 2020 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Google and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2022 version differs from the 2020 version in the following ways: Reorganized the document into clearer sections, simplified language around what users can expect and what Google can do, and added more explicit content rules and warranty/liability disclaimers. Comparison: policies.google.com/terms/archive/20200331-20220105.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Google to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20220105?hl=en-US . The previous version is available at https://policies.google.com/terms/archive/20200331?hl=en-US .

**Service Name:** Microsoft Services Agreement

These terms govern your relationship with Microsoft and apply to the various products and services they offer, which can be found on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Microsoft, they can use it to operate and improve their services, train their AI and machine learning systems, and share it with third parties, but only following your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** Microsoft's Privacy Policy governs how they collect and process your personal data, but these terms don't discuss the details. You can find more information about their data collection and processing on their website.
* **Dispute Resolution:** You and Microsoft will attempt to resolve disputes through binding arbitration, which means you won't have a choice to take the case to court, and class-action lawsuits are generally not allowed. However, you can opt out of this process within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** Either you or Microsoft can terminate the agreement, subject to specific conditions described in the live document.

**Harmful Clauses:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration:** You and Microsoft are forced into binding arbitration, which some users may find problematic. This can limit your right to seek court justice and may result in higher arbitration fees.
* **Class-Action Waivers:** You won't be able to unite with others to bring a class-action lawsuit against Microsoft.

**Other Notes:**

* Some Microsoft services, like Xbox, have specific sign-in and support terms that may need to be reviewed separately.
* Trial offers can automatically renew, so be sure to check the terms to know what you're getting into.
* If you have any questions or concerns, you can contact Microsoft through their published legal contact information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — MICROSOFT SERVICES AGREEMENT (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Added a new 'exportable data' subsection under Your Content, clarified that some services may have separate support terms, added language that some trial offers may require auto-renewal, and updated Xbox service-specific terms regarding sign-in to non-Microsoft platforms. Documented in Microsoft's Updates page (servicesagreement/Updates).
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ . The previous version is available at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/upcoming.aspx .

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Microsoft and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added clarifications around moderation/enforcement with a link to external policy pages, expanded Xbox section to address third-party platforms tracking and sharing user data, and updated the kids-on-Xbox subsection regarding family settings on third-party platforms.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Microsoft to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/Updates . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023*/https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/servicesagreement/ .

**Service Name:** OpenAI Terms of Use (consumer)

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service apply to your relationship with OpenAI, the company behind the AI technology behind various products and services. The terms are effective as of 2024 and provide a guide on how OpenAI uses your content, handles disputes, and terminates agreements.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** You grant OpenAI the right to use your content (such as text, images, or other materials you submit) to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems. This is subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** OpenAI cross-references its published Privacy Policy, which outlines the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most provisions require **binding arbitration** (a private dispute process instead of going to court), with a **class-action waiver** (you can't join a group lawsuit). This is optional for new accounts, with a 30-day **opt-out window**.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions described in the document.
* **Contact:** For questions about the terms, refer to OpenAI's published legal contact information.

**Harmful Clauses to the User:**

* **Mandatory Arbitration and Class-Action Waiver:** This clause can limit your ability to seek justice in a public court and join a group lawsuit, even if your rights are being violated.
* **Binding Arbitration:** This process can be costly and may not provide the same level of protection as a court of law.

Please note that the Terms of Service contain other provisions that may impact your use of OpenAI's services. It's essential to read the full document or consult with a lawyer for a comprehensive understanding of your rights and obligations.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI TERMS OF USE (CONSUMER) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Split the consumer Terms of Use from a separate Business Terms (for API/Enterprise) effective January 31, 2024, switched arbitration provider from ADR Services to National Arbitration and Mediation, and revised the dispute-resolution and batch-arbitration procedures. Documented at help.openai.com/en/articles/8541945.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/row-terms-of-use/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://openai.com/policies/terms-of-use .

**OpenAI Services Agreement (Business/API)**

The OpenAI Services Agreement is a contract between you (the user) and OpenAI that governs the use of their business and API services. This document is effective as of 2025 and replaces the previous terms.

**Key Provisions:**

### Scope

These terms apply to the products and services described on OpenAI's official terms page, including API, ChatGPT Enterprise, and other business services.

### Content and License

When you submit content to OpenAI, they can use it to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.

### Privacy

The terms reference OpenAI's published Privacy Policy, which outlines the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.

### Dispute Resolution

In the event of a dispute, most provisions require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

### Termination

Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions outlined in the live document.

### Flags for Harmful Clauses:**

*   **Data Use:** OpenAI may use your submitted content to train their AI/ML systems, which could raise concerns about data ownership and control.
*   **Binding Arbitration:** The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to participate in class-action lawsuits and seek collective justice.
*   **One-Sided Termination:** The agreement allows either party to terminate the agreement, which could give OpenAI flexibility to end the agreement without much notice or cause.

Overall, these Terms of Service provide a general framework for the use of OpenAI's business and API services, but users should carefully review the document and consider seeking legal advice if they have specific concerns.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — OPENAI SERVICES AGREEMENT (BUSINESS/API) (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with OpenAI and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Replaced the prior Business Terms with a single OpenAI Services Agreement effective May 31, 2025, covering API, ChatGPT Enterprise, ChatGPT Team and other business services, with updated provisions on data handling, indemnification and SLAs. Announcement: community.openai.com/t/new-openai-services-agreement-effective-may-31-2025/1249405.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by OpenAI to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://openai.com/policies/services-agreement/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://openai.com/policies/business-terms/ .

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms of Service govern your relationship with Anthropic and apply to its products and services, as described on its official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You agree that Anthropic can use your submitted content to operate and improve its AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.

* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes are to be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination:** Either party can end the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Warning Flags:**
* **Class-action waivers:** This means you may not be able to join a lawsuit with others who have similar claims against Anthropic.
* **Binding arbitration:** While this can be faster and less expensive than court, it's a private process where you may not have the same protections as in a court of law.

**Additional Information:**
* For questions about these Terms, see Anthropic's published legal contact information at the TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Updated effective October 8, 2025: clarified scope (Claude.ai, Claude Pro, Claude apps), added explicit Acceptable Use Policy reference, refined provisions on business/enterprise email-domain linking, and updated dispute-resolution and governing-law sections. Versioning tracked at tostracker.app/document/anthropic.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2024/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/consumer-terms .

**Summary:** These terms govern the relationship between Anthropic and users of the company's commercial API products and services.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms apply to the specific products and services listed on Anthropic's official terms page.
* **Content and License**: Anthropic uses user-submitted content to improve, operate, and train its AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: These terms cross-reference Anthropic's Privacy Policy, which outlines the types of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most provisions require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. Users can opt-out of arbitration within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to conditions outlined in the live document.

**Clauses to Consider Carefully:**

* **Indemnification**: Anthropic has updated its indemnification policy, which may impact users' responsibilities in cases where Anthropic is sued.
* **Acceptable Use**: The terms are tied to Anthropic's published Usage Policy, which may limit user activities.
* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit users' ability to bring collective action lawsuits.

Please note that these terms are subject to change, and it's essential to review the contract carefully and any subsequent updates before using Anthropic's services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ANTHROPIC COMMERCIAL TERMS OF SERVICE (API) (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Anthropic and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Added more detailed sections on customer data and outputs, clarified that customer prompts and completions are not used to train models by default, and updated indemnification and acceptable-use language tied to the published Usage Policy.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Anthropic to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/2023/https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms .

response:
**Overview**

These are the updated Terms of Service for Facebook and its parent company Meta. The main purpose of these terms is to outline the relationship between Meta and its users. The key provisions cover how user-submitted content is used, how Meta collects and processes user data, and how disputes are resolved.

**Key Provisions**

* **Using Meta's Products Implies Agreement**: By using Meta's products like Facebook, you agree to these terms. This means that if you don't like these terms, you might want to consider not using the service.
* **Content License**: You give Meta permission to use your submitted content (like posts, photos, or videos) to operate, improve, and train its artificial intelligence (AI) and machine-learning (ML) systems.
* **Data Collection and Processing**: Meta collects user data as described in its Privacy Policy. While the terms don't specify what type of data is collected, the Privacy Policy is a separate document that outlines this information.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you disagree with Meta or have a problem, you'll generally need to go through binding arbitration instead of a court. This is a private dispute process where a neutral third-party decides the outcome. However, users can opt-out of this requirement within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination**: Either Meta or the user can end the agreement if specified conditions are met.

**Clawback Warning: Class-Action Waivers**

One potentially troublesome clause is the requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers. This means that users can't join a group lawsuit against Meta even if other users have similar complaints. This can limit the ability of users to seek collective redress, which may result in smaller or fewer settlements.

**Red Flag: AI/ML Processing Without Clear Safeguards**

Another point of concern is the fact that Meta's AI and ML systems can process user content without clear safeguards in place. This means that the more a user engages with the platform, the more data Meta collects and the greater the potential for biased or unintended system actions on these collected data.

**Where to Find More Information**

For questions or concerns about these terms, visit Meta's official website at the provided URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms. The previous version of these terms is available here: https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FACEBOOK / META TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Facebook) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective January 1, 2025: tightened opening agreement language ('using these products means you agree'), added clearer license framing for content uploaded to Meta Products, and added wording about Meta's use of AI/machine-learning systems on user content for service improvement and safety.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Facebook) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.facebook.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.facebook.com/terms .

The Terms of Service document applies to Instagram, a social media service provided by Meta.

Here's a plain-language breakdown of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **What the Terms Cover:** The terms describe your relationship with Meta (the company behind Instagram) and apply to all services listed on their official terms page.
* **Copyright and Usage:** You grant Meta a non-exclusive license to use, distribute, and modify any content you upload to Instagram across the globe.
* **Data Processing:** Meta can use your content to improve and train its AI/ML systems, as long as it follows your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** Instagram's Privacy Policy explains what personal data is collected and how it's processed. You should check this policy for more information.
* **Disputes:** Most issues will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). You can opt out within 30 days of opening your account (excluding new accounts at Steam, which does not use arbitration).
* **Termination:** Either you or Meta can terminate the agreement under the conditions found in the live document.

**Clauses that May be Harmful to the User:**

* The worldwide non-exclusive license for your content may be unrestricted in this Terms of Service document. It is advisable to consult their Privacy Policy which is referenced to understand how your data is being used.
* The binding arbitration clause (5) with class-action waivers means that you agree to settle disputes through private arbitration, bypassing the court system. This restriction might limit your ability to join group lawsuits or participate in class actions.

**Additional Notes:**

* Please find questions about these terms or their application at the Instagram Help Center at https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — INSTAGRAM TERMS OF USE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Meta (Instagram) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Aligned with the Meta umbrella update effective January 1, 2025: explicit grant of a worldwide non-exclusive license to use, distribute and modify uploaded content, and new wording referencing AI features and data processing across Meta Products.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Meta (Instagram) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://help.instagram.com/581066165581870 .

SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — X TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with X (Twitter) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective November 15, 2024: added an explicit, royalty-free, worldwide license for X to use posted content for training machine-learning and generative-AI models, removed the prior in-product opt-out language, and broadened third-party data-sharing permissions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by X (Twitter) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://x.com/en/tos . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240515000000*/https://twitter.com/en/tos .

**Service Name:** TikTok Terms of Service (US)

These Terms of Service govern your relationship with TikTok, a social media platform where users can create, share, and access short-form videos.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to the products and services listed on TikTok's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You grant TikTok a license to use your content to operate, improve, and train its artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) systems, as long as your settings and applicable law permit.
* **Privacy:** The terms cross-reference TikTok's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process your personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** If you have a dispute with TikTok, you may be required to go to binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with no class actions allowed (unless you opt out within 30 days of creating your account).
* **Termination:** You or TikTok can terminate the agreement at any time, subject to specific conditions.
* **Contact:** For questions, see TikTok's published contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Generative-AI rules:** You are responsible for ensuring your inputs and outputs comply with TikTok's rules on generative AI, including not stripping watermarks or claiming AI-generated content is human-made.
* **Restrictions on content:** TikTok may use your content without compensating you, as long as it is for non-commercial purposes (like training its AI/ML systems) and complies with your settings and applicable law.
* **Binding arbitration:** You may be required to go to private arbitration with no class actions allowed, which can be less favorable to you than going to court.

Please note that I've flagged these clauses as potentially harmful, not because they are undoubtedly detrimental, but because they may limit your rights or impose significant burdens on you.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — TIKTOK TERMS OF SERVICE (US) (Effective 2026; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with TikTok and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Effective January 22, 2026: contracting party changed to TikTok USDS following the US joint venture; added explicit generative-AI rules (output 'as is', user responsibility for inputs/outputs, prohibition on stripping watermarks or claiming AI output is human-made); reaffirmed sublicensable license to use content for training ML models.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by TikTok to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.tiktok.com/legal/page/us/terms-of-service/en .

The Terms of Service are for YouTube, a video-sharing service owned by Google.

Here's a summary of the key provisions:

* **Scope**: These terms apply to your relationship with YouTube and its services.
* **Content and License**: When you upload content to YouTube, you grant the company permission to use it to run the platform, improve it, and train its AI systems. This is subject to your personal data settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy**: YouTube's Privacy Policy (a separate document) explains how your personal data is collected and used.
* **Dispute Resolution**: If you have a dispute with YouTube, you may need to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court). This process has a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement, but you should review the live document to understand the conditions.

As for clauses that may be harmful to the user:

* **Monetization of your content**: YouTube has the right to monetize most of your videos, including non-Partner videos, which means you might not maintain control over ads on your content.
* **AI training**: While YouTube uses your content to train its AI systems, it's worth noting that you may not be able to access or control the data used in this process.
* **Class-action waiver**: The binding arbitration process has a class-action waiver, which means you may not be able to participate in a group lawsuit against YouTube.
* **Limited disputes resolution options**: If you disagree with YouTube, you may have limited options for resolving the dispute, as arbitration can result in a private process rather than a public court trial.

Please note that these points are based on the provided Terms of Service, and it's essential to review the document for the most up-to-date information.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — YOUTUBE TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2021; replaces the 2019 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with YouTube and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2021 version differs from the 2019 version in the following ways: Effective June 1, 2021 globally: introduced YouTube's right to monetize most videos (including non-Partner videos), banned collection of facial-recognition data from videos, and updated US tax-withholding obligations for non-US creators. Summary at support.google.com/youtube/answer/10090902.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by YouTube to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20191101000000*/https://www.youtube.com/static?template=terms .

The Terms of Service govern Adobe's agreement with its users, and the name of the service is Adobe General Terms of Use.

Here's a plain-language summary of the key provisions:

* **What Adobe can do with your content**: Adobe can access your user-submitted content, including images, files, and other data, for various purposes like operating its services and training AI/ML systems. However, Adobe explicitly states it does not use your cloud content to train generative-AI models.
* **How Adobe uses your data**: Adobe uses personal data to operate, improve, and train AI/ML systems. It cross-references its published Privacy Policy for exact details on what data is collected and how it's processed.
* **How to resolve disputes**: Most users are required to engage in binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers. This means you may be giving up your right to join class-action lawsuits or participate in group disputes. There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts if you want to avoid this.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under specific conditions described in the Terms of Service.
* **Contact information**: If you have questions or issues, you can find Adobe's legal contact information on their website.

I would flag the following clauses as potentially concerning for users:

* **Binding arbitration and class-action waivers**: This provision could reduce your ability to participate in group disputes or join class-action lawsuits.
* **Access to your content**: While Adobe explicitly states it won't use your cloud content for training generative-AI models, it can still access your content for other purposes. Clarify with Adobe the methods used to improve services and software.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ADOBE GENERAL TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Adobe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: February 2024 update added language allowing Adobe to access user content via 'automated and manual methods' to improve services and software. After backlash in June 2024, Adobe rewrote sections in clearer language, explicitly stating it does not train generative-AI models on customer cloud content and added a plain-English summary of changes.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Adobe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20231101000000*/https://www.adobe.com/legal/terms.html .

* **Scope**: These terms apply to all LinkedIn products and services, as listed on the official terms page.

* **Contact**: For questions or concerns, you can find LinkedIn's contact information at their published legal page.

Keep in mind that these Terms of Service might change over time, and it's essential to review them periodically to ensure you're comfortable with any updates.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — LINKEDIN USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with LinkedIn and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: November 20, 2024 update added explicit references to use of member data and content to train generative AI models for LinkedIn features (with an opt-out toggle in Settings). Also updated dispute-resolution and class-action waiver provisions.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by LinkedIn to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.linkedin.com/legal/user-agreement . The previous version is available at https://www.linkedin.com/legal/previous-user-agreement .

**Service Name:** Discord Terms of Service

The Discord Terms of Service outline the rules and guidelines for using Discord's products and services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Scope:** These terms apply to all Discord products and services, including the official Discord website.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Discord, the company can use it to operate, improve, and train its AI systems. They'll do this based on your settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** Discord's Privacy Policy explains how they collect and process your personal data. You can view this policy on their website.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Discord requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a class-action waiver. This means you can't join a class action lawsuit against Discord. However, you have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to opt out of this requirement.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, but the conditions for this are listed in the live document. I can't provide more information without knowing the exact text.
* **Contact:** If you have questions about these terms, check the company's website for published legal contact information.

**Potential Concerns:**

* The arbitration clause with a class-action waiver may be limiting for users seeking justice in a group or collective manner. However, it's worth noting that users have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.
* When Discord uses your user-submitted content, it may be subject to their AI training processes. This raises questions about data ownership and the responsibility to users. However, this clause is standard practice in many online communities.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — DISCORD TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Discord and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: August 2025 update modernized arbitration language, added new sections on AI-generated content and Discord's use of metadata to train safety systems, expanded the Paid Service Terms, and refreshed Community Guidelines references. Summary: discord.com/safety/important-policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Discord to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://discord.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240601000000*/https://discord.com/terms .

These Terms of Service are for GitHub, a service that allows users to create and share software with others.

Upon reviewing these Terms, the key provisions are:

* **Scope**: These Terms apply to GitHub's products and services, as listed on their official terms page.
* **Content and License**: When you submit content to GitHub, they use it to improve their services, train AI/ML systems (but only according to your settings and applicable law).
* **Privacy**: Your personal data is subject to their published Privacy Policy, which outlines how they collect and process it.
* **Dispute Resolution**: You must use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with a 30-day opt-out window when you first create an account (Steam is not subject to this agreement, but note that other services may include these provisions).
* **Termination**: Either party can end the agreement under certain conditions described in the Terms.
* **Contact**: If you have questions, see their contact information at this link: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service

We flag the following clauses as potentially concerning for users:

* **Data sharing with affiliates**: In March 2026, GitHub expanded how they share your data with Microsoft and other affiliates for AI/ML model development. This may not be ideal for users concerned about data ownership.
* **Using data for AI training**: The Terms now explicitly mention that GitHub uses your data to train AI features. This could be a concern for users worried about their data being used for commercial purposes.
* **Binding arbitration**: We previously mentioned that binding arbitration can be a limitation for users. In this agreement, it's still a requirement with a 30-day opt-out window.

Please note that these Terms of Service are just a summary, and the actual document provides more details. It's always a good idea to review the full text for yourself before using a service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — GITHUB TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2026; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with GitHub and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2026 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: March 2026 update expanded the Affiliates section so personal data may be shared with Microsoft and other GitHub affiliates for AI/ML model development, added a new product-development purpose for using personal data to train AI features, and clarified that user opt-out preferences propagate to affiliates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by GitHub to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://docs.github.com/en/site-policy/github-terms/github-terms-of-service .

**Service Name:** PayPal User Agreement

The Terms of Service govern your relationship with PayPal and cover the products and services listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These terms apply to the products and services offered by PayPal. They take effect as soon as you use PayPal's services.
2. **Content and License**: When you use PayPal, you agree to let them use your submitted content to improve and train their AI/ML systems (this is subject to your settings and applicable law).
3. **Privacy**: The terms reference PayPal's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process personal data.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: You'll resolve disputes with PayPal through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court). There's a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts to avoid this. Note that some contracts and purchases may be exempt from arbitration (like Steam, a notable exception).
5. **Termination**: Either you or PayPal can terminate the agreement (terms not specified here).
6. **Contact**: If you have questions, you can contact PayPal using the information on their website.

**Clauses that may be Harmful to the User:**
* **Dispute Resolution (Clause 5)**: Binding arbitration can be a disadvantage to users as it may limit their ability to seek redress through traditional courts.
* **Termination (Clause 6)**: The terms don't specify the conditions for terminating the agreement, which may leave users unsure of their rights.

Please review these terms carefully before using PayPal's services.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PAYPAL USER AGREEMENT (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with PayPal and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: Multiple 2024 updates: revised seller-protection criteria, added new fee schedules for cross-border transactions, expanded the dispute resolution / chargeback flow, and clarified handling of cryptocurrency holdings. PayPal publishes upcoming and historical policy diffs at paypal.com/us/legalhub/policy-updates.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by PayPal to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/useragreement-full . The previous version is available at https://www.paypal.com/us/legalhub/upcoming-policies-full .

service_name: Apple Media Services Terms and Conditions
response:
The Terms of Service apply to Apple Media Services. Here's a summary of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* These Terms govern your relationship with Apple and apply to Apple services like Apple Music, App Store, and iCloud.
* Apple may use your content to improve its AI and machine learning (AI/ML) systems, but only in accordance with your settings and applicable law.
* Apple requires binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) to resolve disputes, with some exceptions (like Steam).
* You may terminate the agreement if you don't comply with these Terms.
* Apple may terminate the agreement for "any other reason in its sole discretion."

**Provisions that May Be Harmful to the User:**

* **Binding Arbitration:** While Apple provides a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, this provision may limit your options for resolving disputes outside of a private arbitration process.
* **Termination:** Apple may terminate the agreement for any reason, without providing much notice or explanation.
* **Data Use:** While Apple cross-references its published Privacy Policy, this provision may not explicitly address how your content, such as music or movies, is used for Apple's AI/ML systems.

**Other Notes:**

* These Terms describe the company's content-license scope across services, which may include using user-submitted content to train AI/ML systems.
* The updated Terms added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features.
* The Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections have been revised.
* You can find Apple's published Privacy Policy and contact information at the provided URL.

Keep in mind that this summary does not constitute legal advice and is based solely on the provided Terms of Service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — APPLE MEDIA SERVICES TERMS AND CONDITIONS (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Apple and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added explicit references to Apple Intelligence and on-device generative-AI features, clarified content-license scope across services (iCloud, Apple Music, App Store), and revised Family Sharing and Subscriptions sections.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Apple to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/us/terms.html .

**Service Name:** iCloud Terms and Conditions

**Summary:**

These Terms of Service outline the relationship between you, the user, and Apple, the company providing the iCloud service. The agreement applies to various Apple products and services listed on their official terms page.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms govern your relationship with Apple and cover the products and services mentioned on their official terms page.
* **Content and License:** iCloud uses your submitted content to improve its services, train AI/ML systems, and operate its services, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy:** The company's published Privacy Policy outlines the categories of personal data collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most disputes must be resolved through binding arbitration with class-action waivers. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts.

7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/icloud/en/terms.html . **Service Name:** The Snap Terms of Service (also known as the Terms of Use for Snapchat)

**Summary:**
These terms outline the relationship between you and Snap (Snapchat) when using their products and services. They govern how your content is used, shared, and protected, as well as your rights and obligations.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Content and License**: When you submit content to Snapchat, it may be used to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: The terms cross-reference Snapchat's Privacy Policy, which explains what data is collected and how it's processed.
* **Dispute Resolution**: Most disputes will be resolved through binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court) with class-action waivers.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions, as described in the live document.
* **Contact**: For questions, see the company's published legal contact information.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the users:**

* **Dispute Resolution**: The requirement for binding arbitration with class-action waivers may limit your ability to join a class-action lawsuit if you're part of a larger group of users with similar issues.
* **Termination**: The agreement can be terminated under certain conditions without much explanation or notice, which may leave you without access to your account or services.

**Remember**: These terms apply to products and services described on Snapchat's official terms page, so be sure to check there for the most up-to-date information.

It's essential to review the full terms of service for detailed information on your responsibilities and Snapchat's obligations. If you have questions or concerns about these terms, contact Snapchat using the information provided.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — SNAP TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2025; replaces the 2024 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Snap (Snapchat) and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2025 version differs from the 2024 version in the following ways: Effective April 7, 2025: added new sections on My AI and other generative-AI features, expanded the user-content license for Live/Local/crowd-sourced services, clarified data-sharing with parents (for under-18 users via Family Center), and updated arbitration pre-dispute notice procedures.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Snap (Snapchat) to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.snap.com/terms . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20240101000000*/https://www.snap.com/terms .

**Service Name:** Pinterest Terms of Service (2024 version)

These terms outline the agreement between you and Pinterest, covering your use of Pinterest's products and services. Here's a breakdown of the key provisions:

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These terms apply to all Pinterest products and services, as listed on Pinterest's official terms page.
* **Content and License:** You grant Pinterest a license to use your submitted content to operate, improve, and train their AI/ML systems, subject to your account settings and applicable laws.
* **Privacy:** The terms refer to Pinterest's published Privacy Policy, which explains how they collect and process personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** Most provisions require binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court), with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts. This means you may be giving up your right to a court trial.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement, subject to the conditions described in the live document.

**Flagged Provisions:**

* **Dispute Resolution Clauses:** The requirement for binding arbitration and class-action waivers may be detrimental to users, as it can limit your ability to seek justice through the courts.

**Other Noteworthy Points:**

* Pinterest may use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, which could be a benefit for users, but may also raise concerns about data collection and usage.
* Advertisers and merchants have clarified obligations, which may impact how they use or represent your content.

**Important Contacts:**

For questions about these terms, refer to Pinterest's published legal contact information at: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — PINTEREST TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Pinterest and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added language permitting Pinterest to use public Pin content to train AI/ML models for recommendations and safety, clarified obligations for advertisers and merchants, and updated arbitration provisions. Pinterest publishes a public archive at policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Pinterest to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-of-service . The previous version is available at https://policy.pinterest.com/en/terms-archive .

**Figma Terms of Service Summary**

These Terms of Service apply to the Figma products and services. **Key Provisions:**

* **Scope**: These terms govern the user's relationship with Figma.
* **Content and License**: Figma uses user-submitted content to operate and improve its services, including training its AI/ML systems. This happens based on your settings and applicable law.
* **Privacy**: Figma's Privacy Policy sets out how personal data is collected and processed.

**Red Flags:**
- **Binding Arbitration**: Many provisions in these terms require binding arbitration, which is a private dispute process instead of court. Please note that this includes a class-action waiver.
* **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement, but the terms don't specify the exact conditions.

**Other Important Points:**

* Figma introduces AI-powered features like "Make Designs" and "Visual Search."
* Figma clarifies that it won't train third-party generative models on customer file content without opt-in.
* Figma updated its security and incident-notification language.

**Next Steps:**

If you have questions, you can find Figma's published legal contact information at [https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/](https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/).

To summarize, these terms are intended to govern the use of Figma services, using user-submitted content for various purposes, with an emphasis on privacy considerations (through cross-referencing with Figma's Privacy Policy). Review the terms to understand your rights and responsibilities as a user.
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — FIGMA TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Figma and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update added Figma AI features (Make Designs, Visual Search) provisions, clarified that customer file content is not used to train third-party generative models without opt-in, and updated security and incident-notification language.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Figma to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.figma.com/legal/tos/ . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://www.figma.com/tos/ .

**Service Name:** 23andMe Terms of Service

**Key Provisions:**

1. **Scope**: These Terms govern your relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services listed on our official terms page.
2. **Content and License**: We use your user-submitted content to operate, improve, and train our AI/ML systems, subject to your settings and applicable law. We might not tell you how your content is used, but we promise to follow your settings and the law.
3. **Privacy**: We cross-reference our published Privacy Policy, which explains what personal data we collect and how we process it. However, some details might not be included here, so be sure to check the full Privacy Policy for more information.
4. **Dispute Resolution**: Unfortunately, most disputes will be resolved through **binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of court)**, which may not be suitable for everyone. We also have a **class-action waiver (meaning you can't join a group lawsuit)**, which may limit your ability to hold us accountable. You have a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts, but make sure you act quickly if you want to opt out.
5. **Termination**: Either party can terminate the agreement with or without reason, subject to the conditions in the live document. We're not sure what those conditions are, but we promise to follow them.

**Clauses that may be harmful to the user:**

* **Mandatory-arbitration clause**: This forces you to use private arbitration instead of going to court, which might not be a fair or transparent process.
* **Class-action waiver**: This makes it difficult for you to join a group lawsuit, which can limit your ability to hold us accountable for any wrongdoing.
* **Shorter dispute-notice window**: We've shortened the time you have to notice disputes, which may make it harder for you to address issues before they escalate.

Let me know if you have any specific questions or concerns about these Terms of Service!
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — 23ANDME TERMS OF SERVICE (Effective 2023; replaces the 2022 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with 23andMe and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2023 version differs from the 2022 version in the following ways: After the October 2023 data breach, 23andMe updated its TOS to add a mandatory-arbitration clause and 30-day opt-out window, requiring users who didn't write to opt out to arbitrate any breach-related claims; also limited class-action rights and shortened the dispute-notice window.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by 23andMe to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/ . The previous version is available at https://www.23andme.com/legal/terms-of-service/full-version/2.0/ .

response:
**Service Name:** Roblox Terms of Use

**Summary:** These Terms of Service outline the rules and guidelines for using Roblox, a platform where users can create and play online games. The agreement spells out what you can and cannot do on the service, as well as how Roblox will handle user-submitted content and personal data.

**Key Provisions:**

* **Scope:** These Terms apply to all Roblox products and services.
* **Content and License:** When you submit content to Roblox, you grant the company permission to use, improve, and train its AI/ML systems using that content, subject to your settings and applicable law. This means that Roblox can use your creations to make their own products.
* **Privacy:** The Terms reference Roblox's Privacy Policy, which explains how the company collects and processes personal data.
* **Dispute Resolution:** In the event of a dispute, users are required to use binding arbitration (a private dispute process instead of going to court) with a class-action waiver. This means you may not be able to join a group lawsuit against Roblox. However, you can opt out of this requirement within 30 days of creating a new account.
* **Termination:** Either party can terminate the agreement under certain conditions, which are described in the live document.

**Potential Concerns:**

* **Content License:** When you submit content to Roblox, you should be aware that the company can use it to make its own products and train its AI/ML systems. This means that you may not retain the rights to your creations.
* **Dispute Resolution:** The binding arbitration requirement and class-action waiver may limit your ability to challenge Roblox's terms or policies in court.
* **Termination:** The Terms do not provide detailed information on what constitutes a "termination under certain conditions." Users should be cautious and review their accounts regularly to avoid unexpected termination.

**Important Contacts:**

* For questions about the Terms of Service, you can refer to Roblox's published legal contact information at [https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846](https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846).
source_tos:
SUMMARY OF UPDATED TERMS OF SERVICE — ROBLOX TERMS OF USE (Effective 2024; replaces the 2023 version)

1. SCOPE. These updated terms govern the user's relationship with Roblox and apply to the products and services described on the company's official terms page.
2. WHAT CHANGED. The 2024 version differs from the 2023 version in the following ways: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
3. CONTENT AND LICENSE. The updated terms describe how user-submitted content is used by Roblox to operate, improve and (where applicable) train the company's AI/ML systems, subject to the user's settings and applicable law.
4. PRIVACY. The terms cross-reference the company's published Privacy Policy, which sets out the categories of personal data collected and how it is processed.
5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION. Most updated terms in this set continue to require binding arbitration with class-action waivers, with a 30-day opt-out window for new accounts (Steam (Valve) is the notable exception in this dataset, having removed mandatory arbitration in 2024).
6. TERMINATION. Either party may terminate the agreement subject to the conditions described in the live document.
7. CONTACT. For questions about these terms, see the company's published legal contact information at the new TOS URL: https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 . The previous version is available at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846 .

- Section 6 termination conditions
[USER_FAVORABLE]

[EXPECTED SUMMARY POINTS]
- The updated terms take effect in 2024 and replace the 2023 version.
- Key change: 2024 update strengthened minor-protection language (default-private accounts under 13, parental-consent flows), updated Robux/DevEx provisions, added rules for Roblox's generative-AI 'Studio Assistant' and avatar-creation tools, and revised arbitration class-waiver section.
- The new terms govern Roblox Terms of Use for users of Roblox.
- Users should review the cross-referenced Privacy Policy to understand data handling.
- The previous version of the terms is available for comparison at https://web.archive.org/web/20230101000000*/https://en.help.roblox.com/hc/en-us/articles/115004647846.
